newsitem.title: USA: Wall St corporate underwriting tops $200 bln in Q3.
newsitem.headline: Wall St corporate underwriting tops $200 bln in Q3.

text.p: It'll take more than higher interest rates and a midsummer slowdown to put a damper on Wall Street corporate underwriting as issuance rose to $205 billion in the third quarter, according to data released on September 30 by research firm Securities Data Co.
Debt and equity issuance was up about five percent from the year-ago level of $195 billion, exceeding the $200 billion level for the third consecutive quarter, the research firm said.
Merrill Lynch and was once again the leading manager for all new debt and equity deals, Securities Data said.
Merrill Lynch was lead underwriter on 258 deals, with gross domestic proceeds of $35.5 billion.
The firm's equity business put in a good performance with underwriting proceeds exceeding $4.7 billion in the period compared with $2.9 billion in the year-prior period, Securities Data said.
Lehman Brothers was the third quarter's second leading underwriter with $26.1 billion in activity from 199 deals.
Salomon Brothers took third place in domestic public underwriting with $23.2 billion from 145 issues.

Mortgage and asset-backed debt securities likewise enjoyed a larger share of the underwriting pie. The group represented nearly 28 percent of all publicly-issued secrutiies in the third quarter compared to 25 percent in the June-ending period.
However, for equity offerings the third quarter was less than memorable, the research firm said.

Not only did total issuance fall by more than 50 percent from the previous quarter, common stock as a proportion of all offerings in the quarter fell to about 10 percent from 17 percent, in the second period, Securities Data said.
Meanwhile, Euromarket issuance of equity and debt proceeds exceeded $99 billion in the sector during the third quarter, compared to $72 billion a year ago, the research firm added.
Second quarter Euromarket issuance was $151 billion.
